entry.name: mc.sfizz~
entry.description: sfizz~ is a player for files in the Sfz format. The format uses simple text files that specify how audio sample files are triggered by MIDI notes and controllers. (Information on the format is available at sfzformat.com .) The object accepts MIDI messages and produces two or more audio outputs. sfizz~ makes use of the open source Sfizz library project that supports a large subset of standard Sfz opcodes

attributes.description: The note number where a Scala scale begins (default 60).

attributes.name: outputs
attributes.digest: Output Count
attributes.description: Sets the number of audio output channels. The minimum is 2 and the maximum is 1024. If you want more than the default stereo outputs, the Sfz file can specify a stereo output pair for a sample or region of samples using theopcode. A value of 0 for theopcode means output channels 1 and 2 in theobject.1 uses channels 3 and 4. If you created an object with 1024 audio output channels, the highest allowable value of theopcode would be 511 (for channels 1023 and 1024). With any larger value of theattribute you'll want to use theobject that combines all outputs into a single multi-channel patch cord.

messages.name: dictionary
messages.digest: Specify Sfz data in Max dictionary format
messages.description: Theobject accepts Max dictionaries to define the current sample mapping. For examples of the dictionary format refer to thetab of thehelp file. The location of audio sample files referenced by a dictionary is more flexible than the Sfz file relative paths used by the standard Sfz format. Refer to the description of theandattributes for more details.The ability to generate sample data dynamically with a patch is one use case for the dictionary feature. You can even send dictionaries towhile it is playing notes; the new data will be utilized once all sounding notes have turned off.

messages.name: int
messages.digest: MIDI note number (left inlet); MIDI velocity (right inlet)
messages.description: You can trigger samples to play with a MIDI note number in the left inlet preceded by a non-zero MIDI velocity in the right inlet. This allows you to connect aobject directly toto trigger notes.

The first two to three numbers are bytes of the MIDI message.supports an extension to standard MIDI with the third velocity value: if this is ainstead of an, it will be interpreted as a "high resolution" velocity value between 0 (note-off) and 1 (maximum velocity).supports audio-rate MIDI connections from theobject.

messages.name: read
messages.description: Whenis followed by a filename,will locate the file in the Max search path and load it as the current sample player specification. With no arguments,will show an open file dialog prompting you to choose an Sfz file.If there are errors in the file they will be reported in the Max window. A sample file referenced in the Sfz file is not a fatal error; missing samples are displayed as warnings.

messages.description: Themessage will reload the previously loaded Sfz file (using themessage).is useful after editing Sfz files with an external text editor.
